findings.finding: Publisher describes twelve independent protagonists, each carrying melodic and virtuoso bravura material; explicitly conceived to be highly virtuosic for every player. No music preview inspected for this version.

grade.basis: Repertoire-expertise calibration of the publisher’s explicit all-player bravura specification: professional-level secure cello technique and a tightly coordinated twelve-part Latin ensemble. Level 8 is justified by independent soloistic responsibility across all twelve desks, rather than by player count itself. No unsupported claims about particular passages or exact range; mode left unsure without notation.

findings.finding: Specialist edition description reports unequal parts: I–III use thumb position and treble clef; IV remains in bass clef with counting and chord difficulties.
Exact Op.15 source lists a seven-page Cello 1 part, Breitkopf plate 17434/IMC 1764. Download route returned a JavaScript redirect; notation was not inspected.

grade.basis: Repertoire-expertise assessment of Klengel’s substantial Romantic variation writing, with an athletic leading cello part and three independent partners: diploma rather than merely advanced study level. Specialist part description corroborates upper-register requirements in the top three parts and a nontrivial fourth part. Whole-work pace is moderate despite faster variations. This is Op.15, not the easier Op.28; numeric calibration is an expert estimate without newly inspected notation.

findings.finding: Directly inspected first music page: six independent staves; cut time, half note 108, two-flat signature. Upper two parts in treble clef, third in tenor clef initially; staggered accented chordal entries, chromatic motion, then first-cello syncopated melody over repeated upper accompaniment and lower pizzicato figures. Preview covers only opening eleven bars.
Publisher identifies six cello parts plus full score, roughly 4 minutes 45 seconds.

grade.basis: Direct opening-score assessment plus cello repertoire expertise: exposed high-register leading melody and brisk syncopated articulation call for advanced control, while repeated accompaniment patterns are more accessible. Six independent rhythmic roles raise coordination demands but do not justify the professional rating of the twelve-part Variações. Level 5 incorporates ensemble precision; no additional blanket ensemble uplift. Two flats alone do not establish the whole-work mode.
